correctness.rationale: Outer-independent Roman domination requires an independent zero set and a label \(2\) adjacent to each zero. In a complete multipartite graph the zero set is therefore empty or contained in one unique part. The zero-free family contributes \((z+z^2)^N\). If zeros occur in part \(i\), the inside labeling is arbitrary except that at least one zero occurs, while every outside vertex is positive and at least one outside vertex has label \(2\). These conditions give exactly the two factors in the displayed sum. Evaluating at one gives the total-function count, and taking the least supported exponent recovers the known minimum \(N-\max_i n_i+1\). A fresh independent exhaustive replay through order six matched the literal OIR definition and the formula.
residual_risks: The theorem counts ordinary outer-independent Roman functions only, not total or double variants.

originality.rationale: The complete accepted-author text of Ahangar, Chellali, and Samodivkin is the exact primary predecessor. It explicitly gives \(\gamma_{oiR}(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_k})=n-n_k+1\) for sorted part sizes and otherwise studies complexity, bounds, and extremal graphs. A full-text search finds no weight-enumerator theorem for the complete multipartite class. Current Resultary searches return the assigned all-function record as the exact hit and no independent stronger census. The audited polynomial therefore refines a directly inspected prior scalar theorem without claiming that scalar minimum as new.

The audited result upgrades that scalar theorem to a compact closed generating function, total count, and complete feasible-label classification. Those data are standard kinds of enumerative refinements in domination-polynomial research and can support coefficient and random-label questions not answerable from \(\gamma_{oiR}\) alone.
